name: Office application started a script interpreter with an encoded command
purpose: Flag the document-to-script execution chain that is common in malicious attachments.
description: Matches process creation where a document application is the parent of PowerShell/cmd/WScript and the command line contains encoded-command markers.

attack.justification: PowerShell execution with an encoded command line is the observable action of Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell.

playbook.what: On {host}, a document application started a script interpreter for {username} using an encoded command.
playbook.why: Documents rarely need to launch hidden scripts. Encoded commands hide what the script does.
playbook.howSure: Medium. In this data set the command is a labelled synthetic fixture. In real data, some legitimate macros behave this way.
next: Decode and read the command line safely (do not run it).
Look for network connections from {host} right after (Hunt page).
verify: The command's purpose is explained or the document is removed.
No follow-on connections to untrusted destinations from {host}.
alternatives: An internal macro that uses encoded commands for legitimate automation.
